channel.title: Northeast Seattle Dispatch
channel.description: Northeast Seattle news, once a week, from the Northeast Seattle Dispatch.

item.title: The council's budget committee starts voting tomorrow, Friday, November 13, at 9:30 AM
item.description: More committee votes follow on November 16 and 19, and the final vote is Friday, November 20.

item.title: Seattle Forest Week runs through Sunday, and this afternoon it plants at Magnuson Park
item.description: Volunteers put in native trees, shrubs and groundcovers from 12:30 to 3:30 PM on the north cross-park trail, just west of the crest of Kite Hill.

item.title: James Turrell's Skyspace at the Henry Art Gallery reopens Saturday, November 14
item.description: Light Reign is the Henry's permanent installation, and the museum is unveiling it to the public that day.

item.title: your block is yours to shovel
item.description: SDOT ran its snow-plow practice on November 2 and 3.

item.title: Whether Seattle still limits how much of a lot new homes can cover now that four homes per lot are allowed
item.description: A reader asked whether Seattle still limits how much of a lot new homes can cover now that four homes per lot are allowed.

item.title: The budget hearing is today, with remote comment at 1 PM and in-person comment at 5 PM
item.description: The Budget Chair's balancing package was scheduled for Wednesday, November 4, at 9:30 AM. Committee votes follow on November 13, 16 and 19, and the final vote is November 20.

item.title: plan the Thanksgiving week's trash
item.description: In 2024 the city skipped collection on Thanksgiving Day and moved the rest of that week's pickups one day later.

item.title: What can be done about losing pharmacies and grocery stores in Northeast Seattle, and how east-west transit to light rail could help
item.description: A reader asked what can be done about losing pharmacies and grocery stores in Northeast Seattle, and how east-west transit to light rail could help.

item.title: Clocks go back one hour at 2 AM Sunday, November 1
item.description: Daylight saving time ends: 2 AM becomes 1 AM and that hour repeats.

item.title: The second half of 2026 property tax is due Monday, November 2
item.description: A mailed check counts if it is postmarked by the due date; online payment carries a service fee.

item.title: Election Day is Tuesday, November 3
item.description: King County takes ballots three ways: by mail, at a ballot drop box, or in person at a vote center.

item.title: The budget chair's balancing package lands Wednesday, November 4, and the public hearing is Thursday, November 5
item.description: Remote comment starts at 1 PM and in-person comment at 5 PM in the Council Chambers at City Hall.

item.title: Street parking by text is on its way
item.description: SDOT started text-to-pay in Pioneer Square and plans it for every paid parking area in the city by early 2027: text PAY to 77447, enter the zone number on the sign, and pay through the link that comes back.

item.title: report the dark streetlight
item.description: From Sunday the evening walk home starts an hour darker, and a streetlight out on your block shows.

item.title: What the best new restaurant in Northeast Seattle is
item.description: A reader asked what the best new restaurant in Northeast Seattle is.

item.title: Councilmembers bring their budget amendments to the table Tuesday through Thursday, October 27 to 29
item.description: Sessions start at 9:30 AM each day.

item.title: Leaves get free pickup all November: up to 10 extra bags on each collection day
item.description: Seattle Public Utilities takes them with your food and yard waste service, leaves only, no food.

item.title: The University Branch library on Roosevelt Way NE now expects to reopen in December, not September
item.description: The branch has its seismic retrofit done, plus a new heating and cooling system, an elevator, accessible restrooms, a new service desk and a renovated meeting room.

item.title: You can ask for a public EV charger at the curb near your home
item.description: City Light and SDOT are taking applications through fall 2027 for up to 200 curbside Level 2 chargers by 2030.

item.title: Coming home from the Eastside late? Two SR 520 exits close at night next week
item.description: Monday to Thursday, October 26 to 29, 10 PM to 6 AM, the westbound off-ramps to northbound I-5 and to East Roanoke Street close for Montlake work.

item.title: clear the drain at the curb
item.description: Leaves on the street clog storm drains and pipes, and the water ponds on the block.

item.title: This weekend, only 1 Line trains stop at U District and Roosevelt
item.description: Shuttle buses replace 2 Line trains between South Bellevue and International District/Chinatown stations today and tomorrow, October 17 and 18, and no 2 Line trains run north of there to Lynnwood. 1 Line trains run every eight minutes; for Bellevue or Redmond, ride to International…

item.title: Sand Point Way NE is one of the first four streets picked for Seattle's new 24/7 speed cameras
item.description: SDOT chose a one-mile stretch between NE 74th Street and Matthews Avenue NE; the exact blocks come later.

item.title: The council is working through a $9.1 billion budget; the next public hearing is November 5
item.description: Councilmembers discuss amendments October 27 to 29 and the chair's balancing package arrives November 4.

item.title: Close your block for Halloween, free, if you apply by Tuesday
item.description: SDOT's Trick-or-Streets permit closes up to three blocks in a row to cars for an event open to the public, any day October 21 to November 2, until 10 PM; cross streets stay open.

item.title: The Seattle Coffee Festival fills Hangar 30 at Magnuson Park next weekend
item.description: October 24 and 25, at 6310 NE 74th Street.

item.title: November 2, not October 31
item.description: The second half of 2026 King County property tax is due Monday, November 2.
